subject.title: MEDIA: tokens inside markdown code fences are silently ignored

question: Should OpenClaw keep fenced `MEDIA:` lines as literal text and add diagnostics, or change the parser contract to extract standalone fenced `MEDIA:` directives as attachments?
rationale: Both behaviors are defensible: the current code protects code examples and transcripts from accidental attachment extraction, while the report shows a real silent message-loss workflow when models wrap final attachment lines in fences.

options.title: Warn-only diagnostic
options.body: Land the linked warn-only PR so current extraction semantics stay stable while operators get a visible log signal for fenced `MEDIA:` skips.

options.title: Extract fenced directives
options.body: Change the parser to lift standalone fenced `MEDIA:` lines into attachments, accepting that code examples containing valid media paths can start delivering media.

options.title: Docs-only contract
options.body: Document that legacy text `MEDIA:` directives must be standalone plain-text lines and leave runtime behavior unchanged.

recommendation.title: Warn-only diagnostic
recommendation.body: Land the linked warn-only PR so current extraction semantics stay stable while operators get a visible log signal for fenced `MEDIA:` skips.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest live review on the linked candidate PR is a changes-requested review from this person, so they are the best available owner for the parser-contract decision.
